action_context_hypothesised_benefit: IPOTESI: a non-covalent KEAP1 binder and an electrophile, each with and without an acute NFE2L2 loss shown adequate at the endpoint time, read on a target set and on the survivors after loss, in one neural class at a time (neurons and astrocytes separately); the survivor-set readout is Winkel's design transplanted, with the electrophile added to the loss arm
compound_or_probe: RA839 or KI-696 (binder, role: probe only if the loss is verified); sulforaphane (comparator; role from germline-null in vivo studies)
identity_status: RA839: structure in the paper, ChEMBL id not obtained (HTTP 500); KI-696 as in SCI46; sulforaphane: racemic or R-form unstated in every source read
documented_action_and_limits: RA839 in macrophages only; sulforaphane benefit lost in germline-null brain and spinal cord models (comparator); one partial persistence at 50 mg/kg; neither with an acute loss verified at the endpoint time
functional_comparison: functional comparison: one readout in the dish with a non-cytotoxic exposure, the same for both reagents
mechanism_discriminating_control: loss-alone and reagent-alone arms under the same challenge; Keap1-loss arm; the electrophile at two exposures; the inactive analogues RA889/RA912 of the binder
outcome_favourable: binder and electrophile both lose their effect under adequate loss and the Keap1-loss arm agrees: NRF2 dependence of that endpoint (H1/H3)
outcome_contrary: an effect maintained under adequate loss: an alternative route for that reagent and endpoint (H5); worse viability or network under activation (H6)
outcome_unresolved: a partial or unverified loss; a cytotoxic or far-above-range exposure; only NQO1 read
explanations_not_separated: dependence of the endpoint on NRF2 does not separate NRF2 from other proteins of the pathway; compensation in a germline loss; a global knock-out cannot assign the cell type
